reason: E1 shows oxide layers on a related alloy are mechanically unstable and delaminate under high-temperature wear, supporting the first premise. E3 demonstrates galvanic coupling between dissimilar phases (Mo-depleted vs. Mo-enriched) in a CoCrFeNiMo HEA coating, supporting the second and third premises. However, no cited evidence directly supports the synergistic feedback loop or the super-additive degradation outcome; these remain unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: High-temperature wear mechanically removes or damages protective oxide layers at phase boundaries in HEAs
Exposed dissimilar phases at interphase boundaries form localized galvanic cells
Localized galvanic coupling accelerates anodic dissolution and corrosion at phase boundaries
Enhanced corrosion further undermines oxide integrity, creating a synergistic feedback loop
Combined wear and corrosion yields degradation exceeding the sum of individual processes
